title: Why Do Americans Work So Much? ｜ 为什么美国人工作这么多？

sents.en: How will we all keep busy when we only have to work 15 hours a week?
sents.cn: 如果我们一周只需工作15小时，大家该如何打发时间？

sents.en: That was the question that worried the British economist John Maynard Keynes when he wrote his short essay "Economic Possibilities for Our Grandchildren" in 1930.
sents.cn: 这是英国经济学家约翰∙梅纳德∙凯恩斯在1930年撰写短文《我们孙辈的经济前景》时所担忧的问题。

sents.en: Over the next century, he predicted, the economy would become so productive that people would barely need to work at all.
sents.cn: 他预言，在接下来的一个世纪里，经济将变得极具生产力，人们几乎无需工作。

sents.en: For a while, it looked like Keynes was right.
sents.cn: 有段时间，凯恩斯的预言似乎成真。

sents.en: In 1930 the average working week was 47 hours in the United States.
sents.cn: 1930年，美国平均每周工作47小时；

sents.en: But by 1970, the number of hours Americans worked on average had fallen to slightly less than 39.
sents.cn: 但到1970年，美国人平均工作时长已降至略低于39小时。

sents.en: But then something changed.
sents.cn: 但随后情况发生了变化。

sents.en: Instead of continuing to decline, the duration of the working week remained stable.
sents.cn: 每周工作时长没有继续下降，反而趋于稳定，在近半个世纪里一直保持在略低于40小时。

sents.en: It has stayed at just below 40 hours for nearly five decades.
sents.cn: 到底发生了什么？

sents.en: So what happened? Why are people working just as much today as in 1970?
sents.cn: 为何如今人们的工作量和1970年一样多？

sents.en: There would be no mystery in this if Keynes had been wrong about the power of technology to increase the economy's productivity, which he thought would lead to a standard of living "between four and eight times as high as it is today." But Keynes got that right: Technology has made the economy massively more productive.
sents.cn: 如果凯恩斯错估了技术提升经济生产力的能力，这件事本不足为奇——他曾认为技术将带来“相当于今天四到八倍”的生活水平。

sents.en: According to Benjamin M.
sents.cn: 但凯恩斯这点说对了：技术确实让经济生产力大幅提高。

sents.en: Friedman, an economist at Harvard, the U.S. economy is right on track to reach Keynes's eightfold multiple by 2029.
sents.cn: 哈佛经济学家本杰明∙M∙弗里德曼指出，美国经济正按部就班地朝着凯恩斯所说的“八倍”目标迈进，预计2029年达成。

sents.en: That is a century after the last data Keynes would have had access to.
sents.cn: 那距离凯恩斯所能掌握的最后数据，恰好过去了一个世纪。

sents.en: In a new paper, Friedman tries to figure out why that increased productivity has not translated into increased leisure time.
sents.cn: 在一篇新论文中，弗里德曼试图弄清：为何生产力的提升没有转化为更多的闲暇时间。

sents.en: Perhaps people just never feel materially satisfied, always wanting more money to buy the next new thing.
sents.cn: 也许人们永远在物质上不知满足，总想要更多钱去买下一个新玩意儿。

sents.en: This is a theory that appeals to many economists.
sents.cn: 这是许多经济学家认同的一种理论。

sents.en: "This argument is, at best, far from sufficient," he writes.
sents.cn: “这一论点在最好的情况下也远不充分，”他写道。

sents.en: If that were the case, why did the duration of the working week decline in the first place?
sents.cn: 如果真是这样，那每周工作时长当初为何会下降呢？

sents.en: Another theory Friedman considers is that, in an era of ever fewer settings that provide effective opportunities for personal connections and relationships, people may place more value on the socializing that happens at work.
sents.cn: 弗里德曼考虑的另一种理论是：在能提供有效人际交往机会的场所越来越少的年代，人们或许更看重工作中发生的社交。这一理论有一定支撑——如今许多人把同事视作朋友。

sents.en: There is support for this theory.
sents.cn: 但弗里德曼认为，支持该理论的证据远非定论。

sents.en: Many people today consider colleagues as friends. But Friedman argues that the evidence for this theory is far from conclusive.
sents.cn: 许多劳动者表示，他们更想多陪家人，而不是待在工作上。

sents.en: Many workers report that they would like to spend more time with family, rather than at work. Furthermore, this theory cannot explain the change in trend in the U.S. working week in the 1970s.
sents.cn: 此外，这一理论也无法解释20世纪70年代美国每周工作时长趋势的转变。

sents.en: A third possibility proves more convincing for Friedman.
sents.cn: 对弗里德曼而言，第三种可能性更有说服力。

sents.en: That is, American inequality means that the gains of increasing productivity are not widely shared by everyone.
sents.cn: 那就是：美国的不平等意味着生产力提升带来的收益并未被广泛共享。

sents.en: In other words, most Americans are too poor to work less.
sents.cn: 换句话说，大多数美国人太穷，根本没法少工作。

sents.en: Unlike the other two explanations Friedman considers, this one fits chronologically.
sents.cn: 与前两种解释不同，这一解释在时间线上吻合：二战后的一段时期，美国不平等程度随每周工作时长一同下降；

sents.en: Inequality declined in America during the period following World War II, along with the duration of the working week. But since the early 1970s it has risen dramatically.
sents.cn: 但自20世纪70年代初以来，不平等急剧上升。

sents.en: Keynes's prediction of a shorter working week rests on the idea that the standard of living would continue rising for everyone.
sents.cn: 凯恩斯关于更短工作周的预言，建立在“所有人的生活水平将持续提高”这一设想之上。但弗里德曼说，事实并非如此。

sents.en: But Friedman says that this is not what has happened. Although Keynes's eight-fold figure holds up for the economy as a whole, it is not at all the case for the median American worker.
sents.cn: 尽管凯恩斯的“八倍”数字对整个经济成立，对处于中位数的美国劳动者却完全不适用。

sents.en: For them, output by 2029 is likely to be around 3.5 times what it was when Keynes was writing. This is a bit below his four-to eight-fold predicted range.
sents.cn: 对他们而言，到2029年的产出可能约为凯恩斯写作时的3.5倍，略低于他预测的“四到八倍”区间。

sents.en: This can be seen in the median workers' income over this time period complete with a shift in 1973 that fits in precisely with when the working week stopped shrinking.
sents.cn: 这体现在这一时期中位数劳动者的收入上——1973年的一个转折，恰好与每周工作时长停止收缩的时间吻合。

sents.en: According to Friedman, between 1947 and 1973, the average hourly wage for normal workers (those who were not in management roles) in private industries other than agriculture nearly doubled in terms of what their money could buy.
sents.cn: 据弗里德曼，1947至1973年间，非农私营行业中普通劳动者（非管理岗位）的平均时薪，按购买力计算几乎翻了一番。但到2013年，普通劳动者的平均时薪按实际购买力计算，较1973年水平下降了5%。

sents.en: But by 2013 the average hourly wage for ordinary workers had fallen 5 percent from the 1973 level in terms of actual purchasing power.
sents.cn: 因此，尽管自1973年以来美国人的收入可能上升了，但劳动者实际能买到的东西却变少了。

sents.en: Thus, though American incomes may have gone up since 1973, the amount that American workers can actually buy with their money has gone down. For most Americans, then, the magic of increasing productivity stopped working around 1973. Thus, they had to keep working just as much in order to maintain their standard of living.
sents.cn: 对大多数美国人来说，生产力提升的“魔力”大约在1973年失效，于是为了维持生活水平，他们不得不继续像以前一样拼命工作。

sents.en: What Keynes predicted was a very optimistic version of what economists call technological unemployment.
sents.cn: 凯恩斯的预言，是经济学家所称“技术性失业”的一个非常乐观的版本。

sents.en: This is the idea that less labor will be necessary because machines can do so much.
sents.cn: 其含义是：由于机器能承担大量工作，所需人力将减少。

sents.en: In Keynes's vision, the resulting unemployment would be distributed more or less evenly across society in the form of increased leisure.
sents.cn: 在凯恩斯的设想中，由此产生的失业会以“增加闲暇”的形式，或多或少地均匀分布于整个社会。

sents.en: But Friedman says that, for Americans, reality is much darker.
sents.cn: 但弗里德曼说，对美国人而言，现实要灰暗得多。

sents.en: Americans now have a labor market in which millions of people · those with fewer skills and less education · are seeking whatever poorly paid work they can get.
sents.cn: 如今的美国劳动力市场里，数以百万计技能和学历较低的人，正在寻找任何能得到的低薪工作。

sents.en: This is confirmed by a recent poll that found that, for half of hourly workers, their top concern is not that they work too much but that they work too little. This is most likely not because they like their jobs so much. Rather, we can assume it is because they need the money.
sents.cn: 最近一项民调证实了这点：半数小时工最担心的不是工作太多，而是工作太少。这很可能不是因为他们多热爱工作，我们不妨推断，是因为他们缺钱。

sents.en: This explanation leaves an important question.
sents.cn: 这一解释留下了一个重要问题。如果那些超级富豪——自凯恩斯时代以来从生产力提升中获得超额收益的人——本可以少工作，为何仍在工作这么久？

sents.en: If the very rich · the workers who have reaped above-average gains from the increased productivity since Keynes's time · can afford to work less, why do they continue to work so much?
sents.cn: （事实上，研究显示美国收入最高的人往往工作最多。）弗里德曼认为，对许多高收入者来说，工作是一种“爱的劳作”。他们做的是自己关心、感兴趣的事，多做些未必是负担，对他们而言甚至是一种乐趣。这些高收入者从工作中获得意义，工作也是他们自我认知的重要组成部分。当然，他们所得的报酬也足以让这一切物有所值。

sents.en: (Indeed, research has shown that the highest earners in America tend to work the most.) Friedman believes that for many top earners, work is a labor of love.
